elements.text: You already know how to back it up, review it, and roll it back.

**Works with GitHub, GitLab & Bitbucket**
Public or private repos, including self-managed GitLab. Bring the repo you already use.

**What's a Git access token — and why does Dokk ask for one?**
Dokk doesn't store your documents on our servers. It saves them straight into your own Git repository (GitHub, GitLab, or Bitbucket). That's what keeps your work yours — but it means Dokk needs permission to read and write to that repo on your behalf. A personal access token is that permission: think of it as a scoped, revocable key you hand to Dokk instead of your real password.

**When you need it**

**Opening a public repo?** No token needed — Dokk can read it in view-only mode.
**Opening a private repo,** or saving any changes? You'll need a token. Saving is a Git commit, and only you can authorize that.

I**s it safe?**
Yes. Dokk runs entirely in your browser and talks directly to GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket — your token is never sent to a Dokk server. You choose exactly what it can do (just "read & write repository contents" is enough), and you can revoke it anytime from your Git provider, which instantly cuts off access.

**Creating one takes a minute**
In your Git provider's settings, create a personal access token with repository read + write access, then paste it into Dokk's token field. The Open Document dialog shows the exact token type and permission for whichever provider you're using.
